The Bahi is a traditional Assamese transverse flute made entirely from bamboo, played by blowing air across a side blow hole while controlling pitch through finger holes along the tube. It is one of the oldest melodic instruments in Assamese folk music and is prominently used during Rongali Bihu celebrations. Unlike the rhythm-keeping instruments of the Bihu ensemble, the Bahi carries the melodic layer with its soft, flute-like tone. It is traditionally played by men and is closely associated with pastoral and folk music traditions of Assam.
